title: Quick-deploy sample apps & CLI: minimal streaming + retry patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a set of minimal, production-oriented starter apps and CLI examples that demonstrate: 1) safe retry patterns (idempotency keys, exponential backoff + jitter, global vs per-request timeouts), 2) streaming ergonomics for web and CLI consumers (SSE / chunked HTTP + client helpers, resumable/partial output handling, cancellation/ctx propagation), and 3) integration patterns for Next.js, FastAPI, and a small Go HTTP server plus a cross-platform CLI. Each example must be copy-paste runnable, include a short README, an automated test that validates retry behavior and streaming output ordering, and a CI workflow that builds and publishes the sample to the examples registry. Focus on minimal cognitive overhead for engineers onboarding to Redwood SDKs: single-file examples where reasonable, clear environment variable config, and links to relevant SDK helper functions. Scope does NOT include long-form tutorial content or an exhaustive cookbook; this is a pragmatic starter pack for engineers to deploy in minutes and iterate from there.
acceptance_criteria: Next.js example: server-route streaming SSE implementation with client-side incremental render and a README that documents cancellation semantics.
FastAPI example: async streaming endpoint that demonstrates background task cleanup and well-defined request timeouts.
Go HTTP server: context-aware handler that surfaces partial tokens and respects connection cancellation; small integration test that simulates slow downstream.

CLI example: interactive mode that streams model output with progress indicators, supports --dry-run and graceful SIGINT handling, and an example of batching requests with retry on transient failures.
Retries: sample helper functions for idempotency keys, per-request retry policy config, and examples showing when NOT to retry (non-idempotent calls).
Streaming ergonomics: SDK helper usage patterns for restart/resume, chunk reconciliation, and example error handling patterns used in production.
Automated tests: CI checks that run unit tests for retry logic and an integration test validating streamed output reaches client in order.
Publishing: a GitHub Actions pipeline that builds the examples and publishes a zip artifact and a short site preview (Netlify/Pages) for manual QA.
